terms.gloss: one who lives at another’s table by flattery and jokes; a sponger
evidence: Plaut. Men. 505: Tuom parasītum nōn nōvistī?
Cic. Lael. 98: parasītōrum in cōmoediīs assentātiō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Greek παράσιτος, “one who eats beside another”. A stock character of comedy.

phrases.english: Don’t you know your own sponger?

phrases.latin: quasi mūrēs semper edimus aliēnum cibum
phrases.english: like mice, we are always eating other people’s food
